title: What is pi, and why does every circle share it?
examples: How do you find the circumference of a circle?

items.label: Circumference 62.8 cm
items.ask: How do you find the circumference of a circle?

explain.say: Take a plate 20 centimetres across. Wrap a string round its edge and measure the string. You get about 62.8 centimetres. Look at the two bars: the edge is just over 3 times as long as the width.

draw.text: What is pi, and why does every circle share it?

items.label: Circumference 62.8 cm
items.ask: How do you find the circumference of a circle?

explain.say: The distance straight across the middle is the diameter: 20 centimetres. The distance all round the edge is the circumference. How many times does 20 fit into 62.8?

items.label: Circumference 62.8 cm
items.ask: How do you find the circumference of a circle?

explain.say: About 3.14 times! Now try a coin, a plate and a bike wheel. Big or small, the edge is always about 3.14 times the diameter. See how they all sit on one straight line?

marks.label: Plate 20 cm
marks.ask: Why is pi the same for every circle?

explain.say: That special number is called pi, after a Greek letter. Pi is about 3.14. So circumference equals pi times diameter. A bike wheel 66 centimetres across rolls about 207 centimetres every turn.

marks.label: Plate 20 cm
marks.ask: Why is pi the same for every circle?

explain.say: Well done! Wow: pi never ends and never repeats. Computers have worked out more than 100 trillion of its digits! Challenge: a round table is 1 metre across. About how far is it around the edge?

items.label: Circumference 62.8 cm
items.ask: How do you find the circumference of a circle?

faq.a: Pi is the number you get when you divide any circle's circumference by its diameter. It is about 3.14.

faq.q: Why is pi the same for every circle?
faq.a: All circles are the same shape, just scaled up or down. So the edge grows exactly as fast as the width, and their ratio stays the same.
asks: Is pi the same for big and small circles?

faq.q: How do you find the circumference of a circle?
faq.a: Multiply the diameter by pi. A 20 centimetre plate has a circumference of about 20 times 3.14, which is 62.8 centimetres.
No. Pi is an irrational number: its decimals go on forever without repeating. 3.14 and 22 over 7 are just handy approximations.
asks: How many digits does pi have?

faq.q: How far is it around a 1 metre table?
faq.a: About pi times 1 metre, which is roughly 3.14 metres.

facts: Pi has been calculated to more than 100 trillion decimal places.
March 14, written 3/14 in the USA, is celebrated as Pi Day.
